name: Planes World IR Protocol
purpose: Carries the seven-facet Planes-native world model (identity, situation, relation, behavior, expression, affordance, lineage) across the existing `show` boundary to a world-hosting performer, as typed data rather than a new effect.

coordinates.origin: declared per subject by the situation facet's own `space` field — this build does not fix a single world origin

numericBridge.status: defined (Horizon Phase 0 Build 4, spec §9.4) — a discipline layered on the existing to_host/from_foreign seam plus a declared fixed-point unit convention, not a new numeric mechanism inside the value model
numericBridge.convention: A continuous quantity crossing to a physics/GPU host declares a fixed-point unit: a `unit` name for the quantity's boundary unit, and a `places` integer giving how many decimal places of fixed-point precision the host receives (a `places`-digit fixed point — 10^places host subdivisions per one Planes unit). A field carries `unit`/`places` only when it is such a continuous quantity; a field with neither key crosses through the existing `to_host` boundary exactly as Builds 1-3 already do, unquantized. Integer semantic ticks (`schemaVersion`, `occupancy`, `timerTicks`, and every other `integer`-typed field) never carry a unit — they are boundary-exact already and this build does not touch them. See `world_numeric_bridge.py`/`js/world_numeric_bridge.mjs` for the implementation and the `units` table below for what this build declares.
numericBridge.quantizeOutbound: A value crossing outbound (Planes -> host) is rounded to its declared `places` via the language's own existing `round ... to N places` rule (planes_num.Number.round_to / world_numeric_bridge.quantize) before conversion through the existing `to_host`. The bridge invents no second rounding rule. A crossing whose rounding changes the value's rational carries an `approx` record naming the quantization as provenance, the same shape `sine`/`root` already use; a value already exact at its declared scale crosses unmarked.
numericBridge.quantizeInbound: A value re-entering from the host (Planes <- host, e.g. a Rapier output) is first read back as an exact rational via the existing `from_foreign`'s shortest-round-trip decimal, then pinned to its declared `places` the same way an outbound value is, before it becomes a Planes value a program can read — a raw host float never reaches the exact-rational core claiming an exactness it does not have.
numericBridge.determinism: Two runs are compared for determinism on the semantic canonical form — world_ir.canonical_outcome_string / world_delta.semantic_hash — never on host-rendered floats. A host renderer may legitimately differ in floating-point bit pattern across runs or platforms without that being a determinism failure; only a difference in the semantic canonical form is one.

world-position.description: situation.x / situation.y — a world-space position, quantized to the nearest 0.001 Planes world unit at the host boundary.

unsupportedVersion: A world envelope whose declared protocol version is not this file's `version` refuses the whole envelope before any record is validated. The performer retains its last valid semantic frame and requests resynchronization — it never guesses at an unrecognized envelope shape.
unknownRecords: Unknown optional records produce a parser warning and are ignored; the record they name is absent from the normalized output. Unknown protocol versions and malformed critical records stop envelope application. A known record with a malformed field refuses even when that record is optional — unknown and malformed are different cases.
fallback: If a critical record is missing or malformed, the performer keeps its last valid semantic frame, pauses semantic advancement, and requests a full resynchronization rather than applying a partial critical batch.
